text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are on the eve of what will be one of their biggest games of the season. On Sunday, the Bengals are on the road as they look to keep pace in the AFC North in a battle against the Baltimore Ravens.

Coming off of a bye week, the Bengals are looking up at every other team in the division. A win on Sunday puts the Bengals in a place where they could control their own destiny.

Winning in Baltimore is a tall task. It's even taller when Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is in the lineup. However, the latest injury report from the Ravens may just change the Bengals' game plan.

Jackson Out

The Ravens have announced that Jackson will be out in Sunday's contest against the Bengals. The former league MVP is dealing with an ankle injury that has sidelined him for the last two games.

In four games this season, Jackson has posted a 3-1 starting record and has thrown for 967 yards, six touchdown passes, and just one interception.

Obviously, the Ravens not having Jackson is a brutal blow for them. However, backup quarterback Tyler Huntley has been very serviceable since hearing his name called.

In two starts since becoming the starter for the Ravens, Huntley is 1-1, with a win over the Atlanta Falcons and a loss last week to the Cleveland Browns.

Huntley has done an outstanding job protecting the football in his two starts, throwing zero interceptions. However, he could be facing one of the most dynamic defensive lines he has seen in his short time under center.

Put On The Pressure

Putting pressure in Huntley may be the key to winning the game for the Bengals. Interior defensive linemen Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen may very well be the biggest offseason acquisitions the Bengals have made in quite some time.

It's not just the interior of the defensive line that has impressed this season for the Bengals. Another offseason acquisition, Boye Mafe, has been a shining star on the edge. The Bengals are tied for the sixth most sacks in the NFL this season at 17, and aside from the Detroit Lions, who lead the league in sacks, every team ahead of Cincinnati on the list has played more games this season.

There's a lot on the line Sunday, and the Ravens are going to have to go to war without their best soldier against a Bengals team that is starving to get back on the field.

text:
Three of the biggest names we're keeping an eye on this week when it comes to injured running backs for fantasy football are Saquon Barkley, Breece Hall and Jordan Mason.

All three have missed multiple games in a row, but the hope is that they'll be back out on the field in Week 7.

Before we get to updates on those three players, notable backs who have been ruled out include Jeremiyah Love, Zach Charbonnet and David Montgomery.

Meanwhile, Quinshon Judkins headlines the list of running backs who have been cleared to play after beginning the week on the injury report.

MORE: Fantasy football Week 7 running back rankings

Now, here's our running back roundup going into the weekend.

Saquon Barkley injury update

After missing two straight games with a hamstring injury, there's hope for Barkley in Week 7.

He finally returned to practice this week and has logged two limited showings so far. If he can finish off the week with a full practice on Saturday, it would essentially confirm he's playing.

In what was a good sign earlier this week, the Eagles cut one of their running backs, leaving them with two on the active roster and one on the practice squad.

MORE: Vikings and Eagles considered viable partners for blockbuster trade

Philly normally carries three into gamedays, so that could be an indication that Barkley is expected back. We'll have a better idea of where he stands later on Saturday.

Breece Hall injury update

Hall's quadriceps injury has kept him sidelined for each of the last three games, but he finally made some progress this week with two limited sessions before drawing the questionable tag.

While it was a good sign to see Hall take part in his first practices since the injury, he also wasn't able to log a full session, which tells us he might not be all the way back yet.

The veteran Jets running back is probably a 50/50 bet to play.

Jordan Mason injury update

Mason is attempting to return from a thumb injury that landed him on injured reserve.

He was designated to return this week and logged three limited practices before getting the questionable tag.

The fact that Mason was able to practice in full all three days this week strongly suggests he will play, as do comments from Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell.

MORE: Week 7 sell-high trades – Tyler Shough, DK Metcalf, Kyle Pitts inflated

"We'll talk to Jordan and see, but things are looking positive for him being available," O'Connell told reporters on Friday.

We expect Mason to suit up, but it's possible his workload could be limited in his first game back. He'll be splitting work with Aaron Jones.

Rico Dowdle injury update

After missing time with a toe injury, Rico Dowdle made his return to the field in Week 6.

But he did not practice in full this week, posting three limited sessions en route to a questionable tag. That's actually a downgrade in participation for the Steelers back relative to last week, when he was limited once and full twice.

Even still, we'd say Dowdle has a better than 50/50 shot to play.

Mike Washington Jr. injury update

Mike Washington Jr. saw an uptick in work for the Raiders last week, but he also emerged from the game with foot and back injuries.

After getting in a limited practice on Wednesday, he took a step back and was a non-participant on Thursday and Friday before receiving a questionable designation.

Washington is definitely trending in the wrong direction, and we'd expect him to be inactive as a result.

Jonah Coleman injury update

Looking to return off injured reserve, Jonah Coleman was a full participant in practice throughout the week and drew a questionable tag.

While logging three full practices was already a good sign that he is going to make his return to the field in Week 7, Broncos head coach Sean Payton also said he expects the rookie to play but be on a snap count.

"I'm always mindful of anyone's first game back if it's been past a month, you know, call it the pitch count," Payton said.

Coleman's activation should come down on Saturday.

title: Aaron Rodgers not surprised by NFL's handling of Jalen Hurts injury - Yahoo Sports
description:
Aaron Rodgers is never shy about speaking his mind, especially in debates over how to handle health and medical matters.
"I don't have a close relationship with Jalen," Rodgers said.
Rodgers's disagreements with the NFL's medical protocols were highlighted during the COVID season.
Rodgers said he'd "been immunized" against COVID-19, but after he came down with the disease midseason, it became public that he hadn't been vaccinated, but was instead treated holistically outside league protocols.
While you should take any medical expertise offered by Aaron Rodgers with a grain of salt, you should also question the process behind any health matter the league defends so confidently.
text:
Aaron Rodgers is never shy about speaking his mind, especially in debates over how to handle health and medical matters.

So it's no surprise that Rodgers commented on the recent controversy surrounding Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, who played through what was initially described as a "superficial" blood clot that eventually worsened to the point that his season is over.

"I don't have a close relationship with Jalen," Rodgers said. "Obviously, we're in the quarterback fraternity. You don't want to see anything like that happen to anybody, especially the guy who's throwing the football.

"Obviously, I don't know the whole details about what's going on. I've seen what's been printed. The guy in charge of all that, you know, all things medical at the NFL office, and I haven't always seen eye to eye about things. So I can't say I'm real surprised."

"The guy in charge of all that" Rodgers was referring to is NFL chief medical officer Dr. Allen Sills, who dismissed concerns about Hurts's treatment and the timeline of his reported treatment.

"Any idea or any suggestion that a team physician is ever being influenced by a coach, a general manager, a team owner, it just doesn't happen," Sills said in a five-minute defense of the league's protocols.

"If you're not sitting in that room with that patient and you don't have all the data, if you are speculating as a physician on what should have been done, you are unprofessional and unethical in doing that."

Now, with regard to Rodgers's comments, it feels like a pretty clear case of Heartbreaking: The Worst Person You Know Just Made a Great Point.

Rodgers's disagreements with the NFL's medical protocols were highlighted during the COVID season. Rodgers said he'd "been immunized" against COVID-19, but after he came down with the disease midseason, it became public that he hadn't been vaccinated, but was instead treated holistically outside league protocols. Since then, Rodgers has offered plenty of medical complaints, many aimed at Dr. Anthony Fauci. Rodgers's critique here is, without a doubt, loaded.

That said, questioning what the top doctors in the NFL say about football safety and players' health care is necessary. As Michael Silver at The Athletic pointed out, this is the same NFL that had to pay out a $765 million settlement after a class-action lawsuit accused the league of hiding evidence regarding the dangers of head trauma and concussions for years. They made a whole movie about it.

To hear the top doctor of the NFL claim it's "unethical and unprofessional" for other physicians to speculate on the health of an NFL player and suggest that maybe there are more motives to how the team treats the player beyond their long-term health is simply ridiculous. The league itself acknowledges, without saying it outright, that team doctors may have split motivations—that's why each NFL game now includes an Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant who can call out potential concussions from the sidelines. They are unaffiliated for a reason.

While you should take any medical expertise offered by Aaron Rodgers with a grain of salt, you should also question the process behind any health matter the league defends so confidently.

In most cases, the louder the league's rebuttal, the more necessary it is to understand what really happened.

text:
The limp should have given it all away.

One day after Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson noticeably limped to the podium to speak with the media following Friday's practice, he was ruled out with a high ankle sprain for Sunday's Week 7 game against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Jackson has not played since he was injured shortly before halftime of a Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans.

Lamar Jackson has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Bengals," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account on Saturday. "This marks the third straight game that Lamar Jackson will miss with his high ankle sprain. Tyler 'Snoop' Huntley will start in his place once again."

"Ravens rule QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) out for Sunday's game against the Bengals," The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec wrote on his official X account. "It will be Tyler Huntley for third straight start."

"Ravens ruled out Lamar Jackson (ankle) for Sunday's game against the Bengals," ESPN's Jamison Hensley wrote on his official. X account. "Tyler 'Snoop' Huntley will start his third straight game for Baltimore."

Lamar Jackson: Injury-Prone Pattern Emerging

It's the second consecutive season Jackson has missed multiple games — he missed 4 games in 2025 with a variety of injuries.

The Ravens, 4-2, have a murderer's row of a schedule coming up after playing the Bengals.

Lamar now will miss 3 games with his high ankle sprain," NFL on Prime's James Palmer wrote on X. "Lamar did practice this week which is progress and they waited to see if he could go. A sign he's close. Next 3 games after tomorrow: at Bills, Jaguars (TNF), Chargers (MNF).

Jackson said trying to play through injury issues in 2025 was "dumb, a little bit," so it's no surprise — especially in a contract year — that he's not trying to come back until he's 100 percent healthy.

Tyler Huntley Will Start Third Straight Game

Huntley also played the entire second half in a Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans after Jackson was injured right before halftime. Huntley is 1-1 in his first two starts, with a surprise loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6.

In the last 10 quarters, Huntley is 51-of-72 passing for 429 yards, 3 touchdowns and no interceptions to go with 1 rushing touchdown.

text:
The Philadelphia Eagles and head coach Nick Sirianni entered the 2026 NFL season facing a lot of pressure. Unfortunately, the team has been unable to catch any breaks so far this season.

Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the remainder of the season due to blood clots. There has been speculation that the future of his NFL career could be in jeopardy, although that is far from being legitimately reported.

At this point in time, the future is a complete unknown. No one knows what to expect from the franchise moving forward. Howie Roseman could have some tough decisions awaiting him in the near future.

Entering this week's showdown on Monday Night Football against the bitter rival Dallas Cowboys, the Eagles hold a 2-4 record. They are currently fighting for their season. More bad news came out for the team on Saturday.

Philadelphia Eagles Dealt Brutal Injury News Before Facing Cowboys

As shared by John Clark of NBC Sports Philadelphia, the Eagles will have to play without star wide receiver Devonta Smith and fellow wideout Dontayvion Wicks on Monday night.

Smith has been dealing with a hamstring issue that he was unable to overcome to play this week. Wicks, on the other hand, will be held out due to an ankle injury.

Tanner McKee has already been facing an uphill battle since being forced into action due to Hurts' health issues. Now, he'll be forced to play without arguably his top two playmakers. That will make things difficult against a Cowboys team desperate for a win.

Who will Philadelphia have at wide receiver this week? Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown will be asked to step up in a big way. Makai Lemon, the team's first-round pick in this year's draft, will also be given a much bigger role.

Only time will tell whether or not the Eagles can overcome the latest adversity sent their way. Division rivalry games are already difficult enough. Missing so many key players gives Dallas an edge.

Kickoff on Monday night is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET. Fans will be able to watch the game on ESPN.

text:
The Baltimore Ravens will be without Lamar Jackson for the third consecutive week, as the quarterback continues working his way back from a high-ankle sprain he suffered back in Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans.

Jackson returned to practice earlier this week, for the first time since suffering the injury in the second half against Tennessee, but has been officially ruled out by the Ravens ahead of Sunday's clash with their AFC North rivals the Cincinnati Bengals.

After practicing this week, Jackson spoke with the media about the injury:

"I just know it was a sprain, and it hurt bad," Jackson said as quoted by the official Ravens website. "It was very, very, very, very, very painful.

"Just trying to move how I move," Jackson said. "If I can't do that, I can't help my team. I can't put my team in a situation to win. I feel like I'm doing a disservice, if anything."

Tyler Huntley stepped in for Jackson against Tennessee, and led the Ravens to an overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5. While Huntley was fairly sharp against Atlanta, completing 24-of-32 passes for 201 yards and a pair of touchdowns in the 30-23 win, he completed just 19-of-31 passes for 165 yards and a touchdown as the Ravens lost to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6.

text:
The Dallas Cowboys are heading into Week 7's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles facing what should be viewed as a must-win and should-win game.

Philadelphia is dealing with major injury issues, which includes the concerning blood cot issues for quarterback Jalen Hurt along with wide receiver DeVonta Smith's lingering hamstring injury. Both players will miss Week 7 against Dallas.

The Cowboys had multiple names on the injury report themselves this week, but fortunately, Dallas is looking fairly healthy across the board headed into Monday Night Football.

Good News for George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr.

The Cowboys released their final injury report before Monday Night Football, and some of the team's most important players are good to go for the game.

Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder) and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) are both without an injury designation and will play against the Eagles.

Both players are in a contract year and still have a lot to prove to the Dallas front office. They can't afford to miss any games both for their individual goals and if the Cowboys want any chance at winning the NFC East.

Key Players Returning for Cowboys Defense, Three Players Out

Additionally, the Cowboys are officially getting back some key players on defense ahead of Week 7.

This includes the return of cornerback Cobie Durant and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, both of whom have missed multiple weeks due to hamstring injuries. Durant has been out since getting injured in Week 2's win over the Washington Commanders while Overshown suffered his injury in Week 1 against the New York Giants.

Overshown's return had been anticipated during the week, his healthy status is now official on Saturday's injury report. It comes an ideal time for a Dallas defense that will be without starting linebacker Dee Winters due to an Achilles strain. His status will be one to watch headed into Week 8.

Cowboys wide receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and offensive tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring) are also out for the game.

Two Cowboys Players Still Questionable

The status of Cowboys safety P.J. Locke (foot) and linebacker Marist Liufau (foreman) are both questionable against the Eagles.

It remains to be seen if they will play, but there's no doubt their presence would help the depth of the Dallas defense, a unit that's been banged up all season long.

text:
Seattle Seahawks' running back Emanuel Wilson has stepped up when called upon, helping fill injury gaps and making the most of his opportunities in the backfield.

From his Division II roots to the NFL, here are seven things to know about Wilson’s journey to the league.

1. He started at Johnson C. Smith

Emanuel Wilson began his collegiate career at Johnson C. Smith University where he registered 1,040 yards on 159 carries for 13 touchdowns as a redshirt freshman in 2019, earning him CIAA Offensive Rookie of the Year honors.

2. He transferred to Fort Valley State

Following his breakout season with the Golden Bulls, Wilson transferred to Fort Valley State where he would spend the next three years.

In 2022, Wilson exploded for 1,371 yards on 209 touches, scoring 17 rushing touchdowns and adding two more through the air while becoming the program's first 1,000-yard single-season rusher in 18 years.

His historic campaign was capped by garnering SIAC Player of the Year recognition.

3. He was waived by the Broncos in 2023

As an undrafted free agent after the 2023 NFL draft, Wilson was invited to attend rookie minicamp with the Denver Broncos. But after three days, he was waived and left without a team.

4. He was signed by the Packers

Just about a week after the Broncos passed him up, the Green Bay Packers swooped in and signed the DII alum.

Wilson took advantage of the opportunity and led the NFL with 223 yards rushing in the 2023 preseason, earning him an official spot on the Packers' 53-man roster.

5. He earned his first career start in 2025

Then the opportunity to prove himself arrived in November of the 2025 season.

The former FVSU Wildcat earned his first-career start against the Vikings in Week 12 to fill in for an injured Josh Jacobs. His 107 yards and two touchdowns helped lead the Packers to a dominant 23-6 victory.

In over three seasons in Green Bay, Wilson appeared in 41 games with 1,083 yards and eight touchdowns while serving as the primary backup running back.

6. He signed with the Seahawks in 2026

After his contract with the Packers expired, the Seattle Seahawks picked him up on March 13, 2026.

Once again, Wilson has been tasked with stepping up this season amid an injury-riddled running back room, making his first start in the navy and green on Oct. 4 against the Chargers.

He's appeared in six games with three starts so far as a Seahawk, recording 303 yards on 83 attempts with two rushing touchdowns and another receiving.

7. His godbrother plays at Johnson C. Smith

According to HBCU Gameday, Wilson’s godbrother, Fabian Duncan, is currently a running back at Johnson C. Smith. In the NFL offseason, Wilson returned to Eddie C. McGirt Field to train alongside Duncan, the 2025 SIAC Player of the Year.

Talk about a full-circle moment.

text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Packers running back Josh Jacobs will make his 2026 season debut Sunday against the Detroit Lions after spending the first six weeks on the NFL's commissioner exempt list.

Green Bay added him to the active roster from exempt status Saturday. The NFL took Jacobs off the exempt list Monday.

The NFL's investigation of Jacobs for potential violations of the personal conduct policy following his arrest earlier this year on misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor destruction of property charges remains active, and a suspension could be equal to or greater than the number of games he already missed. The six games he has missed would be credited toward any suspension.

For now, Jacobs is cleared to play.

Jacobs pleaded no contest Sept. 10 to the charges resulting from the May 23 incident with a woman at his home near Green Bay. He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000 and reached a deferred judgment agreement on the property damage charge.

Without Jacobs, the Packers have had the worst running game in the NFL, ranking last in rushing yards per game at 59.8 yards. Jacobs was the Packers' leading rusher the previous two seasons, ranking eighth in the league in combined rushing yards (2,258) and tied for fourth in rushing touchdowns (28) during the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

text:
The All-Pro running back has missed the past two games after being injured in the team's Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, and things have quickly gone downhill for Philadelphia in his absence.

Since the last time Barkley took the field, right tackle Lane Johnson retired, Jalen Hurts went on injured reserve for blood clots with a recovery timeline that likely keeps him out for the rest of the season, and running backs Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley both landed on IR, as well.

Should Barkley return to the lineup, he will do so without wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both ruled out, though tight end Dallas Goedert is good to go after missing the first two practices of the week.

Across Barkley's two fully healthy games this season, he has run for 165 yards with a 5.5 yards-per-carry average. He's notably been held without a touchdown on the campaign thus far.

Philly's offense has rushed for just 22 and 35 yards in the past two games he missed, respectively, so they will certainly be hoping all goes well for Barkley in the lead up to Monday Night Football.

Should he end up missing the contest, Dameon Pierce would likely lead way for the Eagles backfield.

Monday night marks a critical NFC East matchup for the Eagles, who sit at 2-4 with four straight losses but remain right in the thick of a division that's seen teams scuffle across the board.

Philadelphia and Dallas (2-4) kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET on Monday.

text:
In his first four seasons in the NFL with the Tennessee Titans, tight end Chig Oknowko had never missed a game. However, it took him only one game with the Washington Commanders to get injured. He tried to play through the season opener, but missed Weeks 2 and 3 with a hamstring injury.

“Like I said, I’ve never missed a game in my career,” Okonkwo told Bryan Colbert Jr. on Washington’s "Next Man Up” podcast.

“So, I don’t think I’ve even really missed practices. So, just coming in the building and not really practicing, not really being around the guys, it was kind of weird feeling, but just knowing my bad right now is to rehab and get back 100 percent and make sure I’m ready to go and it’s so weird because it happened pregame. Usually, an injury is going to happen in the game in a high-speed rep. But, it was pregame on a three-step slant and just happened, and after that, I had to mentally dealing with that,” Oknowko said. “I was scared coming in even the day after that. I’m like, ‘I wonder what they’re going to tell me about that MRI. I just hope they don’t say, ‘Yo, you got to go to IR.’ I hope they don’t say, ‘Oh, you got to miss this amount of games.’’ They came in and gave me the plan and told me, ‘You could be back in two weeks,’ and that was the best for me. If it’s just two weeks, I can deal with that. But if it was something like six weeks, mentally, now you start thinking. I’m just happy to rehab and get back to 100 percent.”

title: Great Douglas News Highlights Positive Final Week 7 Dolphins Injury Report
description:
Douglas missed the past three games because of an ankle injury he sustained in the Week 2 loss against the San Francisco 49ers and the Dolphins clearly missed him.
It's not ridiculous to say the outlook of this game changes with the return of Douglas.
Despite missing three games, Douglas STILL has the third-most receiving yards of any target on the Dolphins with 113.
The Dolphins currently average 153.6 passing yards per game, the second-fewest in the NFL, just 0.1 yards ahead of the Tennessee Titans.
Douglas isn't the only Dolphins rookie who could make his return against the Jets.
text:
After some extensive time off in the form of a bye week, the Miami Dolphins won't be completely healthy when they take on the New York Jets, but they're getting there.

But they will get back a big piece of their offense for the Week 7 matchup against the New York Jets, with wide receiver Caleb Douglas off the injury report after being a full participant in practice Friday.

Douglas missed the past three games because of an ankle injury he sustained in the Week 2 loss against the San Francisco 49ers and the Dolphins clearly missed him.

It's not ridiculous to say the outlook of this game changes with the return of Douglas. The Dolphins passing offense was one-dimensional without him, with only Malik Washington and Greg Dulcich being consistent targets for Malik Willis, but even that's pushing it.

Despite missing three games, Douglas STILL has the third-most receiving yards of any target on the Dolphins with 113.

Miami is lacking a wide receiver that has as much upside as Douglas has shown so far, even with limited snaps due to the injury. His ability to separate from defenders is unmatched on the roster right now, combined with his speed and agility to get open in a hurry. His return brings size back to the position, with his 6-4 frame being taller than any other wide receiver.

The Dolphins currently average 153.6 passing yards per game, the second-fewest in the NFL, just 0.1 yards ahead of the Tennessee Titans. The group could use a splash of youth to energize it against a Jets secondary that allows only 185 yards per game, the fourth-fewest in the NFL.

Who Else Is Coming Back To The Field?

Douglas isn't the only Dolphins rookie who could make his return against the Jets.

Safety Kyle Louis was listed as questionable for Sunday even though he's currently on the IR, but the encouraging sign here is that he was a full participant in practice Friday after being limited the previous two days. This could be a sign he's ready to return in his first week of eligibility after missing the required four games.

Normally, activating someone from the IR would require a corresponding roster move to stay within the 53-player limit, but the Dolphins are currently at 52.

Running back Jaylen Wright, who's been dealing with a nagging foot injury, also was cleared to play. With that said, Wright has struggled to make an impact as Ollie Gordon's backup, but the Jets' defense hasn't had the best success against rushing offenses - 123 yards per game given up. This could be his best chance yet to contribute.

Rookie tight end Will Kacmarek, who has been dealing with a hamstring injury, specifically noted on Thursday that he'll be ready to play Sunday, and he was cleared on Friday. As mentioned earlier with Wright, attacking the ground might be key for Miami's offense, and Kacmarek has impressed as a run blocker for Gordon thus far.

However, there are a few players on defense who might not play this game. That includes edge rusher Rob Beal Jr., who is listed as doubtful. He had to exit the San Francisco game with a hamstring injury. Before that, he recorded a single tackle against Las Vegas in the season opener.

It's also confirmed that cornerback Reese Taylor will not play Sunday because of a quad injury; he was ruled out.

Linebacker Willie Gay Jr. was back at practice Friday after being out one day with an illness, and he was listed as questionable after being a limited participant.

What About New York's Team?

On the other side, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn is dealing with a significantly larger number of questions in terms of who's playing in this game. The most significant player on the list is running back Breece Hall, who was listed as questionable. He's been dealing with a quad injury suffered against Detroit in Week 3.

Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said that he'd be surprised if Hall didn't play in this game, but the Jets might not want to rush things with Hall, especially because his replacement, Braelon Allen, has done such a great job in his wake with 314 yards and two touchdowns.

A big boost to the Jets' receiver corps will be the return of wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, who is expected to play while dealing with a broken finger. It'll be the first time that Mitchell, Garrett Wilson and rookie first-round pick Omar Cooper Jr. will all be ready to go in the same game since their season opener.

Nose tackle T'Vondre Sweat is dealing with a knee injury but is expected to play Sunday. He's been reliable when healthy, with 15 tackles in six games played. It's a solid contribution for a player who was acquired from Tennessee in a trade that sent Jermaine Johnson to the Titans.

There are a few players officially ruled out: linebacker Kiko Mauigoa (quad), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle), and offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion).

Left guard Dylan Parham is questionable to play in this game with a knee injury that has sidelined him for three games. His backup, Jordan Meredith, has played well in his absence, but it would mean a lot for the Jets to get one of their top linemen healthy once again.

Kene Nwangwu is also listed as questionable, which is a big blow for the special teams. He's been a decent kick returner with 251 yards on 11 attempts but hasn't had an opportunity to break a long run yet this season. If he can't go, Isaiah Williams will likely have to shoulder returning once again for the Jets. It should be noted that Williams had a 78-yard punt return for a touchdown for the Jets' only score in the Dolphins' 34-10 victory at MetLife Stadium last December.

At least the Eagles will have Dallas Goedert on Monday night.

The veteran tight end returned to practice on Saturday afternoon after missing the first two days of the week with a knee injury. Goedert said after practice that he expects to play.

Out: WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring), WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), OLB Nolan Smith (concussion), DB Michael Carter II (abdomen)

Questionable: RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring), OLB Jonathan Greenard (ankle), OLB Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle), OG Landon Dickerson (knee/pec), TE Eli Stowers (quad), TE Grant Calcaterra (back), CB Jakorian Bennett (knee)

NFL

Both Smith and Wicks missed practice all week. The Eagles will go into this game with Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore, Hollywood Brown and Britain Covey as their healthy receivers.

At edge rusher, Greenard began the week as a limited participant but has missed the last two days. Greenard will be a game-time decision. text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants middle linebacker Tremaine Edmunds is out for the season with a torn chest muscle, a source told ESPN on Friday.

Edmunds signed a three-year, $36 million deal with the Giants this offseason. He led the team with 50 tackles and was tied for the club lead with two sacks through six games this season.

New York will also be without outside linebacker Chauncey Golston for the remainder of the season, sources told ESPN. Golston was placed on injured reserve earlier this month with a neck injury.

Edmunds, 28, was hurt on one of the final plays of Sunday's 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints. The team was trying to determine this week if it were something Edmunds could manage. He wanted to play through the injury, but it was determined that would not be possible.

The veteran linebacker was one of the leaders of the Giants' defense. He was on the team's leadership counsel and wore the green dot to make the calls on defense.

Veteran Micah McFadden will take his place and is expected to wear the green dot and communicate directly with defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. The Giants have maintained since the summer that they have three starting middle linebackers on the roster with Edmunds, Arvell Reese and McFadden.

"I think I said early on we have three starters. So, when and if that happens, Micah is ready [to start]," coach John Harbaugh said earlier Friday. "He's a starter, and he'll play really well. He'll be excited for his opportunity."

McFadden has started 36 games in his career. He will be in the middle of the defense Sunday against the Houston Texans (2-4).

The Giants (3-2-1) expect to have cornerback Paulson Adebo return from a knee injury. He was on injured reserve but had his window to return opened earlier this week.

text:
CHICAGO (AP) — The Chicago Bears like their group of tight ends, and the position plays a major role in coach Ben Johnson's offense.

That depth is about to be tested.

Chicago will be without Cole Kmet for the rest of the season after he hurt his right knee on a reception with 5:34 left in Thursday night's 30-24 win over New England. It's the first major injury for Kmet since the Illinois native was selected by the Bears in the second round of the 2020 draft out of Notre Dame.

"He's going to be sorely missed. Really, he's Chicago," Johnson said. "He's been here his whole life and he's a big part of our heartbeat. So, it stinks, it does, I hate it for him, I hate it for his teammates as well. And yet the train keeps rolling along. Someone else has to step up."

Kmet was placed on injured reserve on Friday, and defensive end Montez Sweat returned to the roster after completing his two-game suspension for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing substances policy.

Kmet had just 10 catches for 87 yards and a touchdown in seven games this season, but his value to the Bears (5-2) goes beyond his personal numbers. He has been a dependable blocker for Chicago's potent rushing attack, and his versatility has created more flexibility with how the team deploys the rest of its tight ends.

Kmet's injury comes with Colston Loveland beginning to heat up after a slow start to the season. The second-year tight end has 13 receptions for 134 yards and two touchdowns in his last two games.

"He's come on," Johnson said. "The target share's gone up a little bit. He's done a really nice job. He's getting open."

Kmet's absence likely means a bigger role for rookie Sam Roush, a third-round pick in the draft out of Stanford. The Bears also have Stephen Carlson and Qadir Ismail on their practice squad, and Hayden Large could be activated at some point after beginning the season on injured reserve.

Roush, 23, has three receptions for 33 yards in seven games.

"We've been very pleased with the improvement that he's made over these first seven weeks," Johnson said. "There's a high likelihood that his rep count is going to go up as a result of what's going on here. ... Very smart player. He had some rookie hiccups early in the season, like everybody does, and yet he learns. He doesn't make the same mistake twice."

What's working

Caleb Williams posted another impressive performance in his second game back since being sidelined by a right hamstring injury. He was 22 for 33 for 308 yards and two touchdowns.

Williams became the third quarterback in franchise history to throw for 300-plus yards in back-to-back wins, joining Sid Luckman in 1947 and Billy Wade in 1962.

What needs help

There has been some inconsistency with Chicago's secondary. The Bears allowed Jordan Love to pass for 367 yards and two touchdowns in a 31-7 loss at Green Bay on Oct. 11, and they also struggled with Drake Maye in the win over New England. Maye threw for 321 yards and two TDs.

Stock up

Rome Odunze had three receptions for 63 yards — in the fourth quarter. He had six catches for 79 yards over the previous two games combined.

The 24-year-old Odunze played a major role in Chicago's drive to Cairo Santos' 58-yard field goal with 1:34 left. With the Bears facing third-and-9 from their own 10, Odunze made a terrific catch on a 21-yard gain. After D'Andre Swift lost 2 yards on a first-down carry, Odunze had another 21-yard reception.

Stock down

Jaylon Johnson had a rough night. The cornerback whiffed when he tried to tackle Maye on a 15-yard scramble with 3:32 left in the second quarter. He had a similar issue on Rhamondre Stevenson's 48-yard touchdown reception on the final play of the first half. He also was called for pass interference on New England's last drive of the game.

Injuries

Besides Kmet's departure against the Patriots, Chicago also lost cornerback Malik Muhammad to a toe injury. There was no update on his status on Friday.

Key number

71% — Williams' 71% completion rate ranks second in the NFL among qualified passers, going into this weekend's action. He completed 58.1% of his passes last season.

Up next

The Bears don't play again until they visit Seattle on Nov. 2. The last time the teams played, Jason Myers kicked two first-half field goals to send the Seahawks to an ugly 6-3 win at Soldier Field on Dec. 26, 2024. Following the trip to Seattle, the Bears host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Nov. 8.

text:
The Chicago Bears were dealt a devastating blow on Thursday night after tight end Cole Kmet went down with a knee injury.

Kmet suffered the injury in the fourth quarter of the game against the New England Patriots, and the cart had to be brought out, which was the first sign it was something significant.

Unfortunately, head coach Ben Johnson confirmed that on Friday afternoon, revealing that Kmet has a season-ending knee injury. We're still waiting on the specifics of the issue, though.

"Bears TE Cole Kmet will miss the rest of the season with a knee injury," The Chicago Tribune's Sean Hammond relayed.

"He’s everything we want to be about here. He’s going to be sorely missed. He’s Chicago. He’s been here his whole life. He’s a big part of our heartbeat. It stinks. It does. I hate it for him," Johnson said.

Cole Kmet's uncertain future with Bears

There's a lot of time between now and next offseason, but it's very possible we might not see Kmet play another game with the Bears, which is the only team he has ever known in the NFL.

The former Bears second-round pick has one more year left on his current contract, but it also carries a cap hit of $15.4 million, which the Bears likely aren't going to be keen on keeping on the books, especially after drafting Colston Loveland and Sam Roush in consecutive years.

Kmet's 2027 cap hit went up after the team restructured his deal back in April, so it wasn't always that high.

There is a clear out in the deal, with the Bears being able to cut Kmet for a dead-money charge of $5.4 million and a savings of $10 million, according to Over The Cap.

One possible scenario is the Bears tight end accepts a re-work of his deal and takes a pay cut. We'd say that's more possible now that Kmet will be coming back from a significant injury, which figures to soften his market considerably if he hits free agency.

But a major factor in Kmet wanting to stay will be his role. Chicago might want to give Roush a push to a bigger role than the TE3 job he had before Kmet's injury, in which case Kmet would have to take a lesser role.

But, then again, the Bears run 12 and 13 personnel quite a bit, so there is ample room for Kmet to still see a lot of action, even if Roush's workload increases next season.

At this point, Kmet's chances of staying with the Bears are probably slightly better than 50/50.

The good news for him is that the injury occurred fairly early in the season, so Kmet has a good chance to be ready to roll by the time next season starts.

The Chicago Bears were bracing for the loss of their longest-tenured offensive player, and their fears were realized.

Tight end Cole Kmet suffered what looked to be a potentially serious knee injury midway through the fourth quarter on the last of his three receptions in Thursday night's 30-24 defeat of the New England Patriots. As he neared the sideline and tried to turn upfield, he absorbed significant contact from two New England defenders, though it's possible Kmet's knee was already buckling before the hits were delivered. He immediately grabbed for the joint as soon as the play ended.

All-Pro Patriots safety Kevin Byard, who played for the Bears in 2024 and 2025, came over to check on Kmet while he as loaded onto the cart. Kmet gave an appreciative Soldier Field crowd an enthusiastic thumbs up as he was transported into the tunnel.

“We will know more (Friday), but I don’t think it looked very good," Bears coach Ben Johnson said after the game.

Cole Kmet injury update

Johnson told reporters on Friday, Oct. 23 that Kmet will indeed miss the rest of the season with the knee injury. Chicago will place the veteran tight end on injured reserve.

"He's a big part of our heartbeat. It stinks. I hate it," Johnson said.

What did Caleb Williams say about Cole Kmet?

Chicago quarterback Caleb Williams was clearly affected by the injury to Kmet and vowed to pay back a player who has helped the 2024 No. 1 overall pick through his own NFL trials and tribulations.

“It was tough,” Williams said when asked about Kmet's misfortune Thursday. “I don’t know exactly what it is, but getting carted off is never good. You're at least going to miss some time.

"I don’t have the words to describe what Cole is to me, to this team, to this organization. He's the longest-tenured Bear (on offense), I believe. He's been through it and it's challenging. It's tough. I'll be right there with him through every step of whatever the injury is. Cole’s been there for me every step of the way, through the first year, through the second year, and now through this year. I could only do the same for him."

Bears tight end depth chart

Kmet and second-year man Colston Loveland were listed as co-starters by Chicago, which has other options on the roster but might be compelled to add a veteran now that Kmet's season is over.

New York Giants linebacker Tremaine Edmunds will miss the remainder of the 2026 season with a shoulder injury, The Athletic's Dan Duggan reports.

Edmunds was already listed as out for Week 7's matchup with the Houston Texans. However, he is dealing with a torn muscle extending to his chest, according to ESPN's Jordan Raanan.

The injury occurred late in the Giants' 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints in Week 6. Reaching with his left arm attempting to tackle running back Kendre Miller, Edmunds stayed down on the field after the play.

Edmunds, 28, was in his first season with the Giants. He signed a three-year, $36 million deal in March, days after the Chicago Bears released him to create $15 million in salary cap space.

In six games, Edmunds compiled 50 total tackles with 2 sacks and 3 tackles for loss as the Giants' defensive play-caller. He appeared to be on his way to a ninth consecutive season recording 100 or more tackles, averaging 129 per year.

Edmunds was a Pro Bowl selection in 2019 and 2020 with the Buffalo Bills, who made him their 2018 first-round draft pick (No. 16 overall) out of Virginia Tech.

Micah McFadden is expected to replace Edmunds at one of the Giants' inside linebacker spots alongside rookie (and first-round pick) Arvell Reese. McFadden, 26, has appeared in five games this season, recording four tackles. He started at inside linebacker in 2023 and 2024, averaging 104 tackles per season.

LOS ANGELES -- The Los Angeles Rams could be without both of their star wide receivers this week. All-Pro receiver Puka Nacua did not practice Friday and is questionable for Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders after leaving practice early Thursday with a calf injury.

The Rams placed Davante Adams on injured reserve with a ruptured hamstring earlier this week. Adams is expected to miss six to 10 weeks.

Rams head coach Sean McVay called Nacua's injury "minor" but said he didn't know when or how it happened.

"He felt it where he wasn't able to have some of the power and explosion," McVay said. "He just kind of noticed it, but I don't think he was aware of any sort of specific play that led to it. He took part in a majority of the practice, left and got it checked out."

Adams' injury was expected to shift much of the volume of Los Angeles' passing game to Nacua, who had 129 receptions for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2025 despite sharing the field with Adams for most of the season. Now, the Rams could be without the NFL's reigning leader in receptions (Nacua) and touchdown catches (Adams) from last season.

Nacua missed two games for a hip issue earlier this season before returning for the past three. He bounced back quickly, catching 32 passes for 343 yards and a touchdown in those three contests.

Nacua is in a contract year, as the Rams have held off on paying one of the league's top receivers as he proves he can grow from several off-the-field incidents. A second injury in seven weeks could bring the 25-year-old's future with the team into question, though an absence could also illustrate how much the Rams need him on offense.

If Nacua does not play, the Rams would need to rework a passing game built to lean heavily on Nacua and Adams. They would work with a group that includes Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels. The most productive among them this season has been Mumpfield, who has eight catches for 127 yards and a touchdown. Whittington, Atwell and Daniels have combined for just five catches for 43 yards.

Los Angeles opted not to spend significant resources on another wide receiver this offseason despite needing one after last year's narrow loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship Game. The Rams traded up to draft Daniels in the sixth round out of Miami, but he has been a healthy scratch for all six games. They traded running back Jarquez Hunter to bring back Atwell, a previous starter in Los Angeles, but he has been active for just three games and has caught three passes for 31 yards.

The injuries could lead to more targets for running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, both of whom have flashed as receivers. It could also put a heavier load on the tight ends, though the Rams are missing their top receiving option there in Terrance Ferguson, who is on IR with an ankle injury.

The lack of receiving options for Matthew Stafford should mean a heavier dose of a run game that has been efficient but hasn't seen much volume yet for Williams and Corum.

The injury news has been a wave crashing over the Rams since their 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, which dropped them to 2-4. In addition to Adams, they also placed defensive end Kobie Turner and defensive tackle Poona Ford on IR, with Ford's season being over.

Cornerback Trent McDuffie is also questionable to face the Raiders with a groin injury after not practicing this week and missing last week's game against the Cardinals.

text:
We've been holding our breath ever since Chicago Bears tight end Cole Kmet exited the Week 7 game against the New England Patriots early with a knee injury.

It did not look good right off the bat, as Kmet had to be carted off the field in the fourth quarter after going down. Then, after the game, head coach Ben Johnson admitted it didn't look good.

Now, on Friday, we have the update we were fearing.

Johnson addressed the media on Friday afternoon and confirmed that Kmet has a serious knee injury and it is indeed a season-ending issue.

"He’s everything we want to be about here. He’s going to be sorely missed. He’s Chicago. He’s been here his whole life. He’s a big part of our heartbeat. It stinks. It does. I hate it for him," Johnson said.

Now, one has to wonder if Thursday night might have been the last time we see Kmet in a Bears uniform.

He does have one more year left on his contract in 2027, but he also has a hefty $15.4 million cap number and the Bears have a clear out in his contract. He'll almost certainly need to redo the deal to stay.

What Kmet's injury means for Bears

Losing Kmet is a huge blow for the Bears, and in more ways than one.

Even as the No. 2 tight end behind Colston Loveland, Kmet still sees a big role on offense, as evidenced by his 62% snap share. That's because the Bears run 12 and 13 personnel at the third- and fourth-highest rates in the NFL, per Sumer Sports.

We already know he's a plus pass-catcher, but Kmet is also one of the team's best blockers among skill-position players and the importance of his blocking extends to special teams, and specifically on the field goal unit.

Kmet's injury will push rookie tight end and third-round pick Sam Roush into a bigger role, which is concerning because Roush has seen plenty of struggles during his first season in the NFL.

As a pass-catcher, Roush has dropped two passes, which is 40% of his targets, and he has had issues with blocking at times. To make matters worse, Roush has committed three penalties, according to NFLPenalties.com.

Another tight end is needed

The Bears don't have a fourth tight end on their active roster, so they'll need to add another. Chicago has two options on the practice squad in Stephen Carlson and Qadir Ismail.

The most likely approach will be the Bears promoting Carlson over Ismail given the former's advantage in experience, which will be needed in Chicago's young tight ends room.

Carlson has 28 games of experience under his belt while Ismail has never taken a regular-season snap in the NFL. Carlson isn't going to offer anything as a pass-catcher, but he is a sufficient blocker.

Given the Bears' heavy reliance on tight ends, it would not shock us to see the team bring in more help via free-agent signing or a minor trade, but chances are they'll likely asses things over the next few weeks ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline before potentially making a move.

Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers is weighing in on Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts’ medical situation after Hurts was sidelined for the rest of the season with blood clots in his lungs.

Rodgers said that he’s not close with Hurts, but he’s not surprised at how the situation has gone down.

“We’re in the quarterback fraternity, so you don’t want to see anything like that happen to anybody. Especially a guy who’s still in football,” Rodgers said. “I don’t know all the details about what’s going on. All I’ve seen is what’s been printed. Allen Sills, he’s the guy in charge of all things medical at the NFL office, and he and I haven’t always seen eye-to-eye about things. So, I can’t say I’m real surprised.”

Rodgers and the league butted heads over the COVID-19 vaccine in 2021 when Rodgers tried to convince the league to accept homeopathic treatments as an alternative to getting the vaccine.

The handling of Hurts’ issue has been criticized by many in the football world. Hurts was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot before Philadelphia’s game in London but was cleared to play. After flying back to the United States, he was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis, and blood clots were found in his lungs. Hurts is sidelined for the rest of the season as he goes on blood thinners.

title: Anton Harrison's Injury Could Have Major Repercussions for These 4 Jaguars
description:
The Jacksonville Jaguars were dealt a tough blow on Friday, with reports stating the Jaguars' left tackle is set to miss the rest of the 2026 season due to an ACL injury.

Which Jaguars are set to be most impacted by Harrison's injuty, and why?
Does this mean Faalele is set to enter the Jaguars' starting lineup soon post-bye?
But the Jaguars are now right back into the same situation with Harrison out for the year.
text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Anton Harrison is done for the rest of the season.

The Jacksonville Jaguars were dealt a tough blow on Friday, with reports stating the Jaguars' left tackle is set to miss the rest of the 2026 season due to an ACL injury.

The domino effect from Harrison's injury could be significant for a number of members on the roster as a result. Which Jaguars are set to be most impacted by Harrison's injuty, and why? We break it down below.

Anton Harrison

This one is clear. Harrison was entering an absolutely pivotal 2026 season, not just because he was made the team's blindside protector for the first time but because of the timing of his switch to left tackle. Harrison, who had his fifth-year option picked up for next season, was set to be a potential benefactor from the move to left tackle considering what a strong season could have meant for him when it came to his contract and what the talks at the table look like.

Harrison will of course return in 2027, but he will be coming off an ACL injury and will have just a six-game sample size as an NFL left tackle entering the season. This doesn't mean Harrison can't still play himself into a big-time deal with the Jaguars moving forward, but the situation has seen a major wrench thrown into it. The Jaguars needed this season to see if Harrison was worth extending, and Harrison needed this season to prove he should be one of the NFL's highest-paid tackles. Now, neither side is going to get much clarity entering the 2027 season.

Daniele Faalele

It feels unlikely that the Jaguars will play Daniel Faalele much at the tackle position since he is a more natural guard and has subsequently taken more snaps at the guard position over the course of his career. But Faalele, who the Jaguars traded for during training camp as they sustained a rash of offensive line injuries, has been a healthy scratch for the Jaguars in each game this season as they entered each contest with eight active offensive linemen. With Harrison out, Faalele now becomes OL8.

Does this mean Faalele is set to enter the Jaguars' starting lineup soon post-bye? No, not really. But he will at the very least be active and be closer to stepping onto the field than he was before. Faalele is unlikely to be needed unless the Jaguars sustain more injuries along the offensive line, but he should now at the least be an option for the Jaguars to turn to on game day, especially in jumbo packages since Wyatt Milum's role as the No. 6 lineman may now change.

Patrick Mekari

This could be an interesting development for Jaguars offensive lineman Patrick Mekari, who Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said was getting closer to returning from injured reserve after missing all of training camp and the first six games of the season with a back injury. Mekari has dealt with injuries for most of his time with the Jaguars, but he could give them some very real offensive line depth when he is off injured reserve, especially in the context of the Jaguars' swing tackle spot.

Mekari has nearly 2,000 career snaps at the tackle positions since joining the NFL in 2019, giving him a significantly larger sample size at the tackle position than any of the Jaguars' other in-house options for swing tackle. Mekari has been a disappointment with the Jaguars since becoming their highest-paid free agent of the new regime in March 2025, but the loss of Harrison could give him the chance to prove his worth.

Mekari of course has to get healthy first, but once he is healthy he should give the Jaguars a boost in terms of a versatile and experienced depth option. Considering the Jaguars' top swing tackle, Walker Little, is now the team's starting left tackle, then Mekari has suddenly become much more valuable to the Jaguars than he was at the start of the season.

Wyatt Milum

The Jaguars have not had a ton of need for Wyatt Milum to step into the lineup since they drafted him in the third-round of the 2025 NFL Drafft, but he now looks like he is one snap away from likely becoming the Jaguars' starting right tackle. Milum was set to be the Jaguars' top swing tackle at the start of the season if Cole Van Lanen was set to miss time at the start of the year, which of course did not end up happening. But the Jaguars are now right back into the same situation with Harrison out for the year.

Milum has played just 122 snaps on offense in his career thus far, with many of those snaps coming as an extra offensive lineman in jumbo packages. That is a good bit different than potentially lining up at offensive tackle against some of the best pass-rushers in the NFL, but that is the scenario the Jaguars have now found themselves in. Milum went from a luxury player to a critical part of the depth chart now that Harrison is sidelined for the rest of 2026.

text:
4:07pm: Edmunds has a torn muscle in his chest, a source told ESPN’s Jordan Raanan, who backs Duggan in reporting he is done for the year.

3:08pm: In yet another major blow to the Giants, linebacker Tremaine Edmunds will miss the rest of the season with a shoulder injury, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports. He joins quarterback Jaxson Dart and pass rusher Brian Burns as key Giants who will not return from injuries this season.

Edmunds was a big-ticket offseason signing for the Giants, who brought in the former Bill and Bear on a three-year, $36MM contract to replace the released Bobby Okereke. While playing all 380 of the Giants’ defensive snaps over their first six games, Edmunds piled up 50 tackles (three for loss) and added three quarterback hits, two sacks and a pair of pass breakups. The ninth-year veteran and two-time Pro Bowler has never finished with fewer than 100 tackles in a season, but that streak will come to an end in 2026.

Fortunately for the Giants, their offseason moves to address the off-ball linebacker position went beyond adding Edmunds. They also drafted Arvell Reese fifth overall and re-signed Micah McFadden to a one-year, $3.75MM deal. Reese has held his own alongside Edmunds as a full-time starter, but he will now pair with McFadden. While McFadden suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 1 in 2025, he was a regular starter in the Giants’ defense over his first four years.

McFadden has played just two snaps on defense in 2026, but he will now have an opportunity to reclaim a significant role in Edmunds’ place. Jack Kelly, Malik Harrison and Zaire Barnes, who are primarily special-teamers, and practice squad member Chandler Martin are the team’s other options at the position. With the Nov. 10 trade deadline coming up, Big Blue could look for help to fill Edmunds’ void. At 3-2-1, the Giants are in first place in an underwhelming NFC East and could end up as buyers. They have just over $8MM in cap space, which ranks 19th in the NFL.

Speaking of cap space, the Giants guaranteed Edmunds $23.7MM, including $11.35MM in base salary in 2027. His cap number will climb from $5.56MM to a far less palatable $16.17MM, though releasing him before June 1 would cost the Giants $2.52MM in space and leave them with $18.69MM in dead money. Designating Edmunds a post-June 1 release would leave New York with $15.02MM in dead cap, but the team would pick up $1.15MM in spending room. That’s not to say the Giants will move on from Edmunds, but they could consider it in the wake of an injury-ruined season.

Jeanty is not on the injury report at all, so we assume he's 100%, even though most believe he's not. I guess teams don't have to disclose all injuries after all.

The good news is LAR are missing their leading tackler and punchout artist, Landman, as well as 2 of their DT. An opportunity for Jeanty to have a good game.

Kubiak made it a point to say Thornton is 100% healthy and said he's ready to play but he's not being activated. VinnyB then asked if Thornton would be activated to the 53 next week and got a quick 'no comment' from Kubiak, doesn't reflect well on his chances of returning.

The problem is you have to make room for him on the 53 and there isn't alot of players that aren't contributing on Sundays, and the few that aren't have future roles.

Doesn't make alot of sense to activate him, while having to cut someone else like Cody White who plays ST, if Thornton isn't going to be playing significant snaps on Sundays.

Per google ..

An NFL team cannot place a player on season-ending Injured Reserve (IR) if they are healthy, even after completing a 21-day practice window.

The same foundational rules apply at every stage of the IR process: a player must have a legitimate, documented medical condition to be placed on any version of the Injured Reserve list.

What Happens if the 21-Day Window Expires?

When a player is designated to return from IR and begins practicing, a 21-day clock starts. By the end of those 21 days, the team must make a decision based on the player's health and roster status:

If the player is healthy: The team must activate them to the 53-man roster. If they do not want to use a roster spot on the healthy player, they must release or waive them.

If the team takes no action: If the 21 days expire and the team fails to activate the player, the player automatically reverts to IR for the remainder of the season. Doing this intentionally for a healthy player to "stash" them is a violation of league rules and constitutes roster manipulation.

So, it appears Thornton will be activated to the 53 next week or he'll be waived.

If he's waived I would be shocked if he's not claimed immediately, plenty of teams out there will find space for a WR of his size/speed, young with 2+ years left on a rookie contract.

OTOH if this was Kubiak's plan they probably let him go before the season.

Since they can't IR him (because he's healthy) and Kubiak made a point to say he is, I am now leaning more towards they will activate him and release Cody White, who is a vested vet and isn't subject to waivers. They can then re-sign him immediately to the PS, if he chooses to, and he is then eligible for another 3 game-callups.

Will be interesting to see what they do.

text:
HENDERSON, Nev.-- The Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) are playing host to the Los Angeles Rams (2-4) on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium.

To say the Raider Nation is excited about this football game would be an enormous understatement.

But ahead of the big renewal of the rivalry, the Raiders got some concerning news in their latest injury report.

The Rookie Rusher

Rookie RB Mike Washington Jr. is a key part of the heralded 2026 Silver and Black rookie class, and the fan base has been clamoring for more of him with each successful performance.

Earlier this week, I asked Kubiak, who constantly preaches to his team about earning more reps, if Washington Jr. had earned more; he said yes. The Raider Nation was elated, as they stand united about needing to get the run game going.

Kubiak explained what the Arkansas Razorback had done to earn those reps.

“He's putting the work in, and you see the practice come to life in the game. ”

Late Thursday, Mike Washington Jr. showed up on the injury report and was listed as not participating.

On Wednesday, he was listed with a foot/back injury and was limited, but he did not participate on Thursday. That change is very significant.

What This Means

Klint Kubiak likes to give players opportunities in games after successful practices. While it is not impossible, Kubiak’s track record makes it seem improbable that if Washington Jr. doesn’t practice on Friday, he would play on Sunday. That is purely speculative and not from the team; it is simply an inference from Kubiak’s previous statements and implications.

Search for Significance

Since day one, Washington Jr. has been Ashton Jeanty's backup. But he continues to expand his team's trust in him with each successful play.

I asked QB Kirk Cousins on Wednesday about his maturation and growth into what, at the time, looked like a significant contributor on Sunday. His answer was telling.

“When you see the 30-plus-yard run for a touchdown against the Saints, you see the ability to break away. In practice, it’s hard because you’re not being brought to the ground often. So, until you get to the real thing, it’s difficult to evaluate. I think he’s run hard, and he’s continuing to get comfortable in the offense. I think every week as a rookie, no matter what position you're playing, you’re gaining confidence and earning trust. It’s a building process, and coming up on Week 7, the sample size is getting large enough to build that up.”

I asked OC Andrew Janocko about the rookie’s growth, and his praise was both glowing and telling.

“I think it’s just started by proving it in the practice field, taking it from the meeting rooms to the practice field, taking it from the practice field, and then doing specific things well in a game. When you do that, that’s how a young player earns more reps. He takes it step by step and then applies it onto the field.”

What to Expect

We will learn more late Friday morning when I speak to Kubiak and ask him for an update. The 'Raiders' run game has struggled this season, and Mike Washington Jr. was a big reason for optimism that it would take off.

If Washington Jr. can't go, look for Dylan Laube to get more carries, and possibly for the first time all season, UDFA RB Roman Hemby getting called up for his first regular-season action of the season from the practice squad.

text:
CHICAGO (AP) — The Chicago Bears like their group of tight ends, and the position plays a major role in coach Ben Johnson's offense.

That depth is about to be tested.

Chicago will be without Cole Kmet for the rest of the season after he hurt his right knee on a reception with 5:34 left in Thursday night's 30-24 win over New England. It's the first major injury for Kmet since the Illinois native was selected by the Bears in the second round of the 2020 draft out of Notre Dame.

“He’s going to be sorely missed. Really, he’s Chicago,” Johnson said Friday. “He’s been here his whole life and he’s a big part of our heartbeat. So, it stinks, it does, I hate it for him, I hate it for his teammates as well. And yet the train keeps rolling along. Someone else has to step up.”

Kmet had just 10 catches for 87 yards and a touchdown in seven games this season, but his value to the Bears (5-2) goes beyond his personal numbers. He has been a dependable blocker for Chicago's potent rushing attack, and his versatility has created more flexibility with how the team deploys the rest of its tight ends.

Kmet's injury comes with Colston Loveland beginning to heat up after a slow start to the season. The second-year tight end has 13 receptions for 134 yards and two touchdowns in his last two games.

“He’s come on," Johnson said. “The target share’s gone up a little bit. He’s done a really nice job. He’s getting open.”

Kmet's absence likely means a bigger role for rookie Sam Roush, a third-round pick in the draft out of Stanford. The Bears also have Stephen Carlson and Qadir Ismail on their practice squad, and Hayden Large could be activated at some point after beginning the season on injured reserve.

Roush, 23, has three receptions for 33 yards in seven games.

“We’ve been very pleased with the improvement that he’s made over these first seven weeks,” Johnson said. “There’s a high likelihood that his rep count is going to go up as a result of what’s going on here. ... Very smart player. He had some rookie hiccups early in the season, like everybody does, and yet he learns. He doesn’t make the same mistake twice.”

What's working

Caleb Williams posted another impressive performance in his second game back since being sidelined by a right hamstring injury. He was 22 for 33 for 308 yards and two touchdowns.

Williams became the third quarterback in franchise history to throw for 300-plus yards in back-to-back wins, joining Sid Luckman in 1947 and Billy Wade in 1962.

What needs help

There has been some inconsistency with Chicago's secondary. The Bears allowed Jordan Love to pass for 367 yards and two touchdowns in a 31-7 loss at Green Bay on Oct. 11, and they also struggled with Drake Maye in the win over New England. Maye threw for 321 yards and two TDs.

Stock up

Rome Odunze had three receptions for 63 yards — in the fourth quarter. He had six catches for 79 yards over the previous two games combined.

The 24-year-old Odunze played a major role in Chicago's drive to Cairo Santos' 58-yard field goal with 1:34 left. With the Bears facing third-and-9 from their own 10, Odunze made a terrific catch on a 21-yard gain. After D’Andre Swift lost 2 yards on a first-down carry, Odunze had another 21-yard reception.

Stock down

Jaylon Johnson had a rough night. The cornerback whiffed when he tried to tackle Maye on a 15-yard scramble with 3:32 left in the second quarter. He had a similar issue on Rhamondre Stevenson's 48-yard touchdown reception on the final play of the first half. He also was called for pass interference on New England's last drive of the game.

Injuries

Besides Kmet's departure against the Patriots, Chicago also lost cornerback Malik Muhammad to a toe injury. There was no update on his status on Friday.

Key number

71% — Williams' 71% completion rate ranks second in the NFL among qualified passers, going into this weekend's action. He completed 58.1% of his passes last season.

Up next

The Bears don’t play again until they visit Seattle on Nov. 2. The last time the teams played, Jason Myers kicked two first-half field goals to send the Seahawks to an ugly 6-3 win at Soldier Field on Dec. 26, 2024. Following the trip to Seattle, the Bears host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Nov. 8.

text:
CHICAGO -- Bears tight end Cole Kmet will miss the remainder of the 2026 season after he suffered a serious right knee injury during Chicago's 30-24 win over New England, coach Ben Johnson announced Friday.

The Bears placed Kmet on season-ending injured reserve following testing Friday morning after he was unable to bear weight on his leg. In seven games, Kmet had 10 catches for 87 yards and a touchdown.

"He's everything we want to be about here," Johnson said. "He's one of the glue guys. He's one of the guys that I can count on, whether it's a messaging standpoint or getting the pulse of the team. He's going to be sorely missed."

With 5:46 to play in the fourth quarter, Kmet caught an 8-yard pass from Caleb Williams before colliding with Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez and linebacker Robert Spillane as he ran up the Bears' sideline. The tight end immediately grabbed for his knee and had to be carted to the locker room.

Current and former teammates, including Patriots safety Kevin Byard III, gathered around Kmet as he was loaded onto a cart. He gave the crowd a thumbs-up as he was transported through the northwest tunnel inside Soldier Field.

"It stinks, it does. I hate it for him. I hate it for his teammates as well," Johnson said. "And yet the train keeps rolling along. Someone else has to step up."

Kmet, 27, was drafted by the Bears in 2020 and has missed only one game over his seven NFL seasons. He has logged the eighth-highest snap count on offense (62.19%) this season and joined Hall of Famer Mike Ditka on Thursday as just the second tight end in franchise history to top 3,000 career receiving yards after he caught three passes for 28 yards.

He saw a role shift since Johnson took over in 2025 but remained a vital piece of the Bears' operation despite his production as a pass catcher dipping.

Without Kmet, Chicago will lean into Colston Loveland and rookie Sam Roush. Other options further down the Bears' depth chart are Stephen Carlson and Qadir Ismail on the practice squad and undrafted free agent Hayden Large, who is eligible to come off injured reserve.

The Bears play some of the highest rates of 12 and 13 personnel (multiple-TE sets) in the NFL. While Kmet's absence will undoubtedly be felt in a multitude of ways, Johnson said the offense won't change, particularly what it asks of its tight ends.

"We trained all our tight ends to be able to do all the jobs," Johnson said. "I don't see us really changing who we are or what we do as a result of that. ... There's a lot of solutions out there to make sure that we can still run the ball, pass protect and our route running, I think we're gonna be OK."

Jacksonville Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison will miss the remainder of the season after tearing a ligament in his right knee.

Harrison is Jacksonville's first starter to sustain a season-ending injury in 2026.

text:
The Dallas Cowboys are dealing with an injury at wide receiver that opens the door for one of the team's preseason superstars to make his NFL debut in Week 7.

That injury is to wide receiver and returner KaVontae Turpin, who is dealing with a ribs injury he suffered in Week 6. Turpin did not take part in practice on Thursday.

Furthermore, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports that Turpin is dealing with "cartilage damage" and will "probably" miss at least this week, when the Cowboys face the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night.

"Cowboys receiver/returner KaVontae Turpin suffered an injury to his ribs Sunday, and one source believes he's dealing with cartilage damage," Fowler wrote.

"He will probably miss this week and go from there," he added.

Time for Camden Brown's debut?

The Cowboys have carried five receivers into gamedays for every contest this season. Turpin being ruled out would lessen that number to four, unless they dress Camden Brown, who has remained inactive for every game this season.

Dallas' offense has sputtered of late. Perhaps the Cowboys should not only dress Brown, who was electric during the preseason, but also give him some snaps.

Brown also has special teams experience after playing in that area during the preseason, so that gives him added value and a better chance to finally see the field in Week 7.

Camden Brown's electric offseason

An undrafted free-agent signing of the Cowboys after the 2026 NFL Draft, Brown was a menace against Dallas defense in camp (that doesn't hold as much weight as it once did with how badly the Cowboys' defense has played, but I digress) and he then carried that into the preseason with electric showings.

The 6-foot-2, 204-pound wide receiver tallied three catches for 62 yards and two touchdowns in preseason Week 1, and followed that up with two catches for 77 yards in the second exhibition contest.

“The game’s not too big for him. He does it every day in practice, we see it all the time," head coach Brian Schottenheimer stated. "Really good day, but he’s got to keep stacking what he’s been doing."

But it wasn't just about the totals for Brown, who made some "this guy belongs in the league" kinds of catches along the way.

Brown cooled off in the final preseason game with just one catch for 27 yards, but he had done enough to state his case and the Cowboys ended up keeping him against all odds because the expectation all offseason was the team would only carry five wideouts with how top-heavy it was.

Cowboys fans have been wanting to see Brown all season long after the impressive display he had during the offseason.

With Turpin likely to sit, it's time to free Camden Brown and let him play some snaps on offense, too.
